limitations_and_boundaries: The human gastruloid model does not show evidence of cell types associated with anterior neural fates, which would be required to form brain tissue.
They do not form extra-embryonic tissues required for implantation.
They lack the morphology of an early human embryo and do not manifest human organismal form.
They are non-intact, non-autonomous, and non-equivalent to in vivo human embryos, and do not have human organismal potential.
Sample sizes were not predetermined; experiments were not randomized and investigators were not blinded.
Different cell lines required different Chiron concentrations, indicating line-specific optimization.
Most gastruloids tended to curl or retract after 72 h, limiting the window of observation.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

experiments_or_tasks: Human ES cells were pre-treated with Chiron (WNT agonist) for 24 h, then seeded in low-adherence plates with Chiron to form aggregates.
Morphology was monitored over 96 h; elongation was quantified by length-to-width ratio and automated classification.

methods.name: Human gastruloid protocol
methods.protocol_description: Human ES cells cultured in Nutristem on vitronectin-coated plates were pre-treated with cell-line-dependent Chiron concentration for 24 h. Cells were dissociated with EDTA, washed, and reaggregated in Essential 6 medium with ROCK inhibitor and Chiron. 400–600 cells per 40 µl were seeded in ultra-low-adherence 96-well plates, centrifuged, and medium was exchanged daily with E6.
